items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: Jimmy and I fell out about those two tunes... we were going to become a team... if you and Sammy were friends when you had nothing

ctx.x: And so does BMI. And so does the union, but they, they, you know,...but I made a lot of records and got nothing. Absolutely nothing. Well I did a thing with Sidney Bechet. I wrote the tune; I said, "Sidney, man, you got half of it.." you know, I'm not liberal. I wrote Same with Jimmy Rushing. /"Leave Me," and "How You Want Your Lovin' Done" on Vanguard. Jimmy and I fell out about those two tunes because...well, what happened was we were going to become a team and Steve Allen wanted us to do a show, you know,…

almost a lodge meeting. And Cliff Grover said, "Well, Jimmy, if you and Sammy were friends when you had nothing, and when you got something you shared together, and then when you get a little more you want it all, that's not fair." But this is the way we , you know what I mean, this is the way we ' . So that's why I try to stay away from writing any songs for anybody, you know what I mean, I do my own thing.
When you got with Decca, you did a lot of stuff also... you did things with gospel singers.
